comment: Pairs not worth attempting again without new information. A null solver blocks the problem for every integration, which is right when the limit is in the reference itself. generation.coverage drops these from the work queue; add an entry when you block a pair, with the evidence that justifies it.

blockers.detail: Z3 could not prove the minimum ruler length for any of the three instances at 180s. A performance limit of this solver on this problem, not a reference or contract fault, so it is blocked for z3_python only. A materially better encoding would justify retrying.

The instance field Qualified is a ragged array: one variable-length list of qualified workers per task. MiniZinc's data interface binds a list of lists as a rectangular 2D array, so the runner fails with 'non-uniform array literal' before solving, whatever the model says. Reshaping the field inside run.py would be the problem-specific converter the integration's skill rules out, so this is an integration limit rather than a modelling one.

Each row of the instance field movies mixes a string title with an integer start and end. MiniZinc's data interface binds a list of lists as a rectangular array of one element type and refuses with "non-uniform array literal. Expected `string' but got `int'", whatever the model says. Same class of obstacle as the ragged Qualified field of covering_opl.

The declared output is the whole ten-digit pandigital number, which is at most 9876543210 and so exceeds the 32-bit FlatZinc integer range Gecode accepts: the parser rejects the model with "The literal '9999999999' of the type int is out of range (-2147483646..2147483646)" before solving. Any faithful model has to represent that value, so this is an integration limit rather than a modelling one. A solver with a wider integer type would not hit it.

The licence bundled with the gurobipy wheel allows 2000 variables and 2000 constraints. The order-7 instance (json:4) needs all 49 cells distinct over 1..49: a one-hot encoding is 2401 binaries, and a pairwise one is 1176 disequalities, each two constraints. The one-hot model passes the four smaller instances and is refused on json:4. A full Gurobi licence would not hit this.

The licence bundled with the gurobipy wheel allows 2000 variables and 2000 constraints. For n = 13 and 15 the output has 26 and 35 triples; stating that two triples share at most one element takes one AND variable per triple pair and element (4225 and 8925), or one per triple and element pair (2028 and 3675). The AND-variable model passes n = 7 and 9 and is refused on n = 13 (json:2). A full Gurobi licence would not hit this.

The CPLEX Community Edition in the cplex wheel allows 1000 variables and 1000 constraints. The order-7 instance (json:4) needs all 49 cells distinct over 1..49: 2401 one-hot binaries, or 1176 pairwise disequalities, each one variable and two constraints in docplex. The one-hot model was refused on json:4 at the gurobipy integration's larger limit of 2000; the full CPLEX would not hit this.

The CPLEX Community Edition in the cplex wheel allows 1000 variables and 1000 constraints. For n = 13 and 15, stating that two of the 26 or 35 triples share at most one element takes 4225 and 8925 AND variables pairwise, or 2028 and 3675 per triple and element pair. The AND-variable model was refused on n = 13 at the gurobipy integration's larger limit of 2000; the full CPLEX would not hit this.

Choco proves the makespan optimum only on the embedded example and the 3-job ragged instance (2 of 5 instances); ft06, la01 and the 6x3 instance each run past the 180 s limit. Two encodings behave the same: pairwise disjunctions on each machine and cumulative constraints of capacity 1. The model was evaluated and accepted on those two instances but not retained. A search strategy or an encoding with stronger disjunctive propagation would justify retrying.

CLP(FD) does not finish the optimality proof on the example, json:2 and json:4 within 180 s: the shipment variables range over 0..100 and no labelling order tried (ff, ffc, leftmost, with down, min or max) proves the optimum in 60 s on the example. The driver reports the abandoned proof on json:4 as no_solution, so the evaluation is a rejection. A model that keeps the shipments off the search or a tighter bound would justify retrying.

After cumulative/2 is given only the jobs of positive length, the 12-job example and one 32-job instance finish, and the other 32-job instance (json:2) does not prove its makespan within 180 s under ff, ffc, leftmost, min or bisect labelling; the driver reports the abandoned proof as no_solution. A stronger encoding of the makespan bound would justify retrying.

Z3 proves the tour length only on the 6-city instance; the 12-city example and the 20 and 30 city instances run past 180 s with a circuit written as arc Booleans and MTZ-style positions. The model was accepted on that one instance but not retained.

The kernel kills the run at the 2048 MB limit on the example: 12 shipment variables over 0..100 need a ladder each for the objective and a wide sum_var for the declared total_cost. A model without the wide ladders would justify retrying.
None of the five instances finishes within 180 s: the 12 shipment atoms range over 0..100 and the optimality proof does not close. A tighter formulation of the shipments would justify retrying.

Attempt 1 hit the 2048 MB limit; attempt 2, with the total price tied to the price sum by one equality over a domain bounded by the budget, ran past 180 s on the example, the only instance. A different encoding of the budget sum would justify retrying.
Two encodings, with derived atoms and with the objective stated on the choice atoms, both ran past 180 s on the example, the only instance.

The cross-multiplied fraction equation grounds past the 2048 MB limit on the example, because the products of the digit atoms are instantiated in one rule body. An encoding that grounds less would justify retrying.

The instance fields alphabet and words_str are strings, and the words are given only inside words_str (a Python-style list printed as one string). Plain ASP has no operation that splits a string into characters, so the letters cannot be recovered from the facts. The only route is an embedded script, and the integration reports 'lua support not available' (Python scripting is unavailable too, per the skill). An integration limit rather than a modelling one.

The instance has a field named _SHIP. solvers/clingo_asp/run.py predicate() lowers only the first character, which is '_', so the runner emits the fact _SHIP(1). Clingo reads an identifier with no lowercase letter after its underscores as a variable, so every program fails with 'parsing failed' before solving, whatever the model says. The mechanism is inferred from the identifier rules and from run.py; the failure itself was measured. Fixing it means changing run.py, which this run may not do.

Ten attempts, none found a solution within the 180 s execution limit on the only instance (every one ended no_instance_verified). Encodings tried: reified pair comparisons, face counts with products, a 12376-row table of dice in two orders, and per-face element/3 counts, each with several labelling orders. clpfd has no clause learning, and stderr diagnostics show that each prefix of the first three dice takes seconds to refute. A performance limit of this solver on this problem; a materially different encoding or a faster search strategy would justify retrying.

The reference has an objective (minimize). The pysat integration declares optimization: false and solvers/pysat/run.py refuses a returned objective ('PySAT solves satisfaction problems only; this problem has an objective'). A single CNF cannot state optimality without embedding the optimum, which is not allowed. A model that returns the objective was refused by the runner. Supporting optimisation (for example through PySAT's RC2 MaxSAT solver) is an integration change, so every objective problem is blocked for pysat until then.

The declared output is the whole ten-digit pandigital number, which is above 2^31-1. The runner reads output atoms with symbol.number and clingo integers are 32 bits, so no atom can carry the value. A model with full ten-digit prefixes ended with no_solution at the overflowing last step; a model that stops at nine digits was rejected as invalid_solution. The 9-digit prefix being correct is inferred, the record does not show it. Same class of obstacle as divisible_by_1_through_9 / minizinc_gecode.

The declared output is the ten-digit number, up to 9876543210. The pysat runner reads an integer output only from an Integer object or a literal, and Integer in this python-sat version builds the whole value range and registers one variable id per value. A bare Integer over 0..10^10 is killed at the 2048 MB limit before any constraint is added. Only a probe attempt was written, since no model can declare the output without the Integer. An integration limit rather than a modelling one.

The answer is a sum of even Fibonacci numbers and needs an output domain of at least 4.6 million values. The pysat runner reads an integer output only from an Integer object, which registers one variable id per value: the coupled encoding over 0..5.3M is killed at the 2048 MB limit and the direct encoding exceeds 190 s. Only probe attempts were written. An integration limit rather than a modelling one.

The CPLEX Community Edition in the cplex wheel allows 1000 variables and 1000 constraints. The 200-car instances need one capacity row per option window, 987 rows on json:1 before any demand row, so a one-row-per-window formulation cannot fit; the model was refused on json:1 with 4800 variables and 1211 constraints. The row count is derived, the refusal measured. The full CPLEX would not hit this.

The licence bundled with the gurobipy wheel allows 2000 variables and 2000 constraints. The counts are derived, the refusal measured. A full Gurobi licence would not hit this.
